GeGI: 3D strip detector simulation¶

32 orthogonal strips, two guard rings, 11 mm HPGe crystal, -879 V bias, and 92.3 K. The full 3D calculation uses 5,068,800 nodes. Dimensions and model inputs are listed in README.md.

Electric potential and field¶

All 34 electrodes enter the 3D solve. The mesh resolves strip gaps and contact faces; the surrounding vacuum extends to x/y = ±55 mm and z = ±12 mm.

Equipotential contours and in-plane field lines are shown on sections through strip centers. Adaptive RK4 traces terminate at contacts or section boundaries. The second figure enlarges the strip gap.

Charge drift¶

Six 662 keV point deposits sample the center, different depths, a strip gap, an active edge and a guard. Solid lines show electrons; dashed lines show holes. The drift time step is 0.5 ns.

Induced charge and current¶

Shockley–Ramo signals for a central 662 keV deposit give approximately ±35.95 fC on the collecting strips, with transient induction on their neighbors. Currents are time derivatives of the induced charge, before electronics processing.

Expected full collected charge magnitude: 35.953929888406776 fC; X09=35.95393; Y09=-35.95393

Collection map¶

The mid-depth scan maps starting positions to collecting strips and guards. White corners lie outside the crystal. Sampling points are offset from exact gap symmetry lines.

Charge sharing and diffusion¶

A Gaussian cloud with σx = 0.10 mm is represented by 48 weighted starting points. Its trajectories separate toward neighboring strips. The sharing curve includes four seeded diffusion realizations using De = 239 and Dh = 279 cm²/s.

Depth timing and temperature¶

Collection-time difference, t_e − t_h, versus depth at 80 and 92.3 K. ADL2016 drift uses Omar1987 temperature scaling with the same electric field and ionized impurity density.

Saved results¶

Figures, tables and solved fields are saved in the results folder. Reload baseline_simulation.jls with deserialize in this project environment.
